model_interpretation.claim: The selected explicit SSE2 parent computes four powers and a sum-of-products for each CND polynomial evaluation. Rewriting that same supplied polynomial in Horner form may reduce SIMD multiply instructions while leaving scalar logf/expf, the Black-Scholes formula, threading and the ordinary serial fallback unchanged. The altered rounding must pass varied-input tolerance checks; it may not improve performance, especially if scalar math remains dominant.

model_interpretation.claim: Replacing three exact SSE2 divisions in the explicit kernel with a reciprocal estimate refined once by Newton iteration may reduce division latency while retaining near-single-precision results. The SIMD arithmetic and CND coefficients remain unchanged; unsafe denominators, exponential ranges, tails and unsupported builds use the scalar implementation. The controller must verify tolerance and measure it against the 7.529 ms ordinary-loop baseline and the 2.662 ms measured SSE2 parent; no speedup is assumed.

items.subject: Compiler-vectorized versus explicit SIMD execution
items.objective: Keep threading unchanged and compare the ordinary per-option loop as compiled by the frozen build with an explicit x86-intrinsics kernel. Use only ISA supported by the frozen target/build, with compile-time guards and a scalar fallback; do not change compiler flags or add runtime environment/ISA probing. Preserve the supplied Black-Scholes computation and CND coefficients. If vector math requires altered rounding, validate it against tolerance on varied inputs and retain a correct fallback. Measure each route separately so G can test combinations with T1 and T3.
